preflight.note: Created before Tauri 2 desktop implementation begins; governed write UX is gated on WI054's proven mutation boundary.

acceptance_criteria.text: Create a Tauri 2 desktop application as a consumer of reusable Rust core APIs; RepoPact repository, validation, analysis, graph, and mutation semantics are not independently reimplemented in the TypeScript/web frontend.
Provide repository/workspace open/switch behavior and typed repository snapshots with dashboard health, work, decisions, evidence, validation, graph, analysis, and settings navigation.

Implement work browsing/detail UX with lifecycle/scope/dependency filtering, search, acceptance-criterion/evidence state, related decisions, frozen-surface implications, relationships, validation, history/context, and advanced raw representation read-only by default.

Implement a guided work-item creation workflow covering intent, deterministic repository analysis, scope/ownership, dependencies, acceptance criteria, evidence plan, governance/frozen-surface review, core-generated mutation preview, and explicit create/apply.

Supported editing renders the Rust core mutation plan before apply, including fields/files/records changed, lifecycle/generated-artifact/relationship impact, diagnostics, canonical diff/preview, and stale-plan state; the frontend has no bypass write path.
Decision UX exposes rationale/state, alternatives/supersession, references, and impact context without altering canonical decision semantics for presentation convenience.

Evidence UX exposes associated work/criteria, run/check/artifact/provenance/validation state and clearly preserves durability/immutability expectations; completed evidence is not presented as an ordinary overwrite editor.
Expose graph/dependency/impact views derived from the core relationship model, with navigation back to source records and no separate frontend persistence authority.

Implement filesystem watching below the UI boundary with debounce/coalescing, path normalization/classification, incremental refresh/revalidation, self-originated mutation handling, and typed repository-change events consumed by the frontend.

Constrain the Tauri 2 command/capability surface to explicit repository-scoped RepoPact operations; do not grant generic arbitrary filesystem write, unconstrained traversal, or unrestricted shell execution to the webview.
The desktop explicitly distinguishes its local application capability boundary from WI050 protected admission/enforcement and never claims equivalent enforcement authority.
Provide modern, accessible, keyboard-usable responsive UI behavior with clear lifecycle/diagnostic states and dark/light themes without sacrificing information density or semantic clarity.
Document and test Windows, Linux, and macOS behavior/packaging constraints to the available execution level; frozen CI/release paths remain subject to their existing separate approval contract.
Any assisted-analysis UI remains provider-neutral and proposal-only; no provider becomes a mandatory RepoPact authority dependency or gains implicit governed-write power.

Closeout evidence demonstrates supported read/browse/analyze/graph/mutation workflows, live refresh behavior, constrained Tauri capabilities, frontend/core semantic separation, cross-platform status, and known deferred surfaces without claiming Python/canonical-core cutover.
